title: From Action Principle to Stochastic Thermodynamics of Elastic and Viscous Active Matter
authors: Valentina Barletta, Michele Lupini, Ian D. Estabrook, Laeschkir Würthner, Isabella R. Graf, Caren Norden, Lamberto Rondoni, Anna Erzberger, Roman Belousov
abstract: Motivated by the complex material properties of living matter, we derive a framework of stochastic thermo- and elastodynamics for active materials from the classical principle of least action and the Rayleighian formalism for external forces. Our approach couples the local barycentric collective coordinate and the streaming velocity as the canonical conjugate pair, which unifies various descriptions of elastic and viscous soft matter, including Helfrich theory for lipid membranes, linear and nonlinear elasticity of thin shells and deformable droplets, as well as hydrodynamics of active and passive fluids. The Lagrangian mechanics of collective field variables permits direct applications of the results and theorems from statistical mechanics to existing models of complex soft and living matter. To illustrate the potential applications of stochastic elastodynamics in biology, we derive and simulate a boundary-driven deformation model of an elastic cell nucleus in the presence of fluctuations.
summary: This paper develops a comprehensive theoretical framework to describe the dynamics of active and viscoelastic soft matter by extending the classical action principle to include stochastic and active forces. It unifies models ranging from lipid membranes to cell nuclei, allowing researchers to analyze complex biological mechanics using tools from statistical mechanics. This work is significant for understanding non-equilibrium processes in living matter.
main_problem: To derive a unifying framework for the stochastic thermo- and elastodynamics of active materials by connecting the classical principle of least action to fluctuating field variables.
main_result: The framework successfully unifies descriptions for various soft matter systems, providing a systematic way to incorporate active forces and thermal fluctuations while maintaining thermodynamic consistency.
method: The derivation starts from the classical principle of least action and the Rayleighian formalism, coupling the local barycentric collective coordinate and streaming velocity as canonical conjugate pairs.
model_or_system: The model applies to elastic and viscous active matter, exemplified by the simulation of a boundary-driven deformation of an elastic cell nucleus. The dynamics are governed by extensions of the Euler-Lagrange equations incorporating active stresses and noise terms.
key_observables: Displacement vector u, streaming velocity v, Hamiltonian H, and entropy production rate.
important_parameters: Active stress parameters ($ ar{\lambda}_t,  ar{\mu}_t$), friction coefficients ($ ar{\gamma}$), and the white-noise limit assumption.
main_assumptions: The approach assumes the applicability of the action principle to fluctuating field variables and utilizes the white-noise limit for the friction term in the stochastic equation.
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates the displacement vector of a body relative to a reference configuration, parameterized by material coordinates.
paper_structure: The paper builds from the classical action principle to derive stochastic elastodynamics, showing how the Lagrangian mechanics allows the application of statistical mechanics theorems to complex soft matter models.
why_interesting: Although focused on classical soft matter, the rigorous application of variational principles and the incorporation of non-equilibrium fluctuations (stochastic thermodynamics) provide powerful theoretical tools relevant to open quantum systems and quantum dissipation models.
